latestSnapshot.readme:
This dataset contains the raw 3 Tesla fMRI data and T1 structural images of 58 children: 22 children with typical reading and spelling skills, 16 children with isolated spelling deficits (SpD) and 20 children with dyslexia. 
This dataset was used for the paper " Reading-related functional activity in children with isolated spelling deficits and dyslexia", which was published in Language, Cognition and Neuroscience (doi: 10.1080/23273798.2020.1859569). 
Stimuli consisted of 60 words and 60 matched pseudohomophones of three to eight letters. Each stimulus was presented alone in white on a black background for 3s in an event-related design. After it disappeared, a fixation cross was displayed. The presentation of the fixation cross was jittered between 2000 and 6000 ms (M = 4000 ms). To prevent fatigue effects in children, stimuli were presented over three consecutive runs of 40 items each, separated by short breaks of 3-5 min. Children were instructed to read aloud the stimuli appearing on the screen.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
EVENTS FILES (corrected in version 1.4.0)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

The events.tsv files distributed up to and including version 1.3.1 were not
correct and should not be used. In each of them two complete 40-trial
schedules were interleaved by onset: the rows labelled W and PH, and a second
set of rows labelled "mispron". Those two sets are the timings of the two
pseudorandomised versions of the task. Since every child was presented with
exactly one version, one of the two sets did not apply to the child in whose
file it appeared, and the applicable set carried no word/pseudohomophone
labels at all whenever the child had been given the second version. The label
"mispron" is not a behavioural code and has nothing to do with
mispronunciation.

All events.tsv files have now been rebuilt from the original Presentation
logfiles, which record, for every trial, the string that was shown, its
length, whether it was a word or a pseudohomophone, and which version was
being run. The version had been hardcoded into the stimulus script before each
run and is recorded nowhere else - not in the DICOMs, the NIfTI headers or
participants.tsv.

Columns:

  onset         seconds from the first scanner trigger of that run. The script
                waited on that pulse before drawing anything, so onset 0 is
                also the start of volume 1 and no shift is required.
  duration      measured on-screen duration, not the nominal one. A "3 s"
                stimulus comes out at about 3.0165 s.
  trial_type    word, pseudohomophone, or fixation. The first two correspond
                to W and PH in the paper and in the previous files.
  stim_word     the letter string that was shown.
  item_id       base-item number, 1-60. The word and pseudohomophone forms of
                an item share an item_id, so the two conditions can be matched
                on phonology; within one version each item occurs twice across
                the three runs, once in each form.
  n_letters     number of characters in stim_word.
  stim_version  which pseudorandomisation the child was given, 1 or 2. It is
                constant within a child across all three runs. A third version
                was prepared but never presented.

Fixation rows are included so that the jittered inter-trial intervals are
explicit; they can be ignored when modelling.

A HED annotation is provided in task-read_events.json at the dataset root, and
validates against HED schema 8.4.0.

Known issues with individual runs:

  sub-047EPKL012017 run 2   The paradigm was aborted after 4 trials, and the
                            EPI stored as run 2 was acquired some 213 s away
                            from when that paradigm ran, so the two are not the
                            same event. The four logged trials therefore do not
                            belong to this scan and no events file is provided.
                            This run should be dropped from analyses.
  sub-047EPKL014067         The events distributed previously were taken from
                            another child's session. Child number 67 had been
                            issued twice, and the logs were paired the wrong
                            way round; the pairing was resolved from the
                            constant offset between the stimulus PC and the
                            scanner clock.
  sub-047EPKL014048 runs 1-2,
  sub-047EPKL011049 run 1   The previously distributed onsets match neither
                            surviving logfile. The files now provided are built
                            from logs that pair correctly with the imaging data.
  sub-047EPKL011041 run 1,
  sub-047EPKL011049 run 2,
  sub-047EPKL012071         No logfile survives, so the version cannot be
                            established and no events file is provided.

In total six runs are left without an events.tsv: the five above and
sub-047EPKL012017 run 2.

Run length varies between 122 and 130 volumes because the EPI was stopped by
hand once the paradigm had finished. Enough volumes were acquired in every run
to cover its last trial.

Responses were spoken aloud into an MR-compatible microphone and recorded to a
separate audio file per trial. They were not scored online and have no logged
onset, so no reaction times or accuracy are available in these files.
